purpose: Section 15/23: full results for the primary safety-critical dimension - creditEligibility.

interReviewerReproducibility.description: Can 3 independent adjudicators reproduce the same CREDIT/NO_CREDIT call on the same evidence?

evaluatorVsIndependentConsensus.description: Does the evaluator's own atomic disposition agree with the independent majority consensus?
evaluatorVsIndependentConsensus.note: Per Section 24, reproducibility and accuracy are two distinct required tests for a safety-critical dimension. creditEligibility passes the first (interReviewer) but fails the second (evaluatorVsConsensus) by 0.64 percentage points (89.36% vs 90% required).

falseCreditControlsCrossCheck.description: All 14 historical false-credit controls: do all 3 adjudicators AND the evaluator's own sealed disposition agree these are NO_CREDIT?
falseCreditControlsCrossCheck.result: ALL 14 PASS - unanimous NO_CREDIT across all 3 adjudicators and the evaluator, with zero regression.
falseCreditControlsCrossCheck.detail: See 18-known-false-credit-controls.json for the full per-case table.

mismatchPatternObservation: 4 of the 5 mismatches are the evaluator being MORE conservative than the independent human-equivalent consensus (evaluator says NO_CREDIT where consensus says CREDIT) - i.e. the evaluator's frozen matcher is stricter about claim-identity correspondence than the median adjudicator, consistent with Workstream A's deliberately conservative sibling-claim-identity discipline (Section 10). Exactly 1 mismatch (doc-a::X::10.01a-us-guaranty) runs the other direction (evaluator more permissive than consensus) and is flagged in 22-remaining-evaluator-risks.json for scrutiny, since an evaluator-permissive/reviewer-strict mismatch is the more safety-relevant failure mode of the two.
conclusion: creditEligibility passes its inter-reviewer reproducibility gate but fails its evaluator-vs-consensus accuracy gate. Per Section 24, BOTH tests are required for a safety-critical dimension to certify; this dimension does not fully certify this phase.
